reading.body:
Delaware passed data center and large energy use facility laws in August 2026, then saw a data center moratorium introduced the following June.

The pattern is a state building out the legal machinery for large power consumers and then facing a push to stop new ones. SB312 amends three titles of the code for data centers, and HB233 amends Title 26 for large energy use facilities. Both passed on the same day, 2026-08-25. SB353, a moratorium on data center development, was introduced on 2026-06-29 and remains introduced. The sequencing matters: the enabling statutes came first, the brake came later, and the brake has not moved.

For AI specifically, the relevant fact is that the binding constraint shows up as land use and utility law, not as technology law. The bills that touch compute directly are about siting and electricity, while the AI-specific measures are narrower: an AI Commission, a regulatory sandbox for agentic AI, and a pilot program for AI and extended reality in schools. The one federal appellate ruling in the record concerns fair use in AI training, and it is a headline, not a Delaware action.

What this does not tell the reader is how much load any of these facilities would draw, whether the moratorium has support, or how the passed laws change permitting in practice. The record is a bill list with statuses and dates. It shows what Delaware is legislating, not what gets built.
